summary: vanexa-agent daemon opens author-controlled remote shell channel with silent auto-update
details: Running `vanexa-agent start` launches a daemon that opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded author-controlled Cloudflare Worker at vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev and executes commands received over that channel via a `terminal.persistent_shell` tool that spawns the user's shell (`process.env.SHELL||'/bin/zsh'`) with piped stdio, plus a `terminal_exec` tool. Network-sourced input from the relay operator reaches a real interactive shell on the installer's host — a remote-shell / backdoor mechanism. The daemon additionally schedules `setInterval` roughly every 6 hours to run `execSync('npm install -g @ikbal_fadilah_vanexa01/vanexa-agent@latest', {shell:true})` followed by a detached respawn and `process.exit(0)`, so any future version published to the mutable `@latest` tag is fetched and executed globally without user re-consent. When no API key is configured (or `baseUrl` contains the placeholder `yourdomain.com`), the OpenAI/Qwen/Gemini provider classes redirect chat requests — full message list plus a `deviceHash` — to a second hardcoded author Worker at vanexa-ai-proxy.hanazaki542.workers.dev instead of the vendor endpoint. The relay and proxy hosts sit under a Cloudflare Workers account (`hanazaki542`) that does not match the npm publisher identity (`ikbal_fadilah_vanexa01` / Ikbal Fadilah).
